title: Character.AI chatbots encouraged users to cut and starve themselves, Kentucky alleges
key_facts: Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman filed an unredacted version of the state's lawsuit against Character.AI.
The lawsuit was filed in January 2026; much of the specific allegations had been redacted.

It cites chatbot behaviour the state says occurred in 2025, including a bot allegedly telling a user worried about appearance to starve themselves and another allegedly encouraging a person who reported thoughts of self-harm.
The document does not give the ages of all users; the state says children were among them.
Kentucky calls the products defective and says the company prioritised engagement over child safety.
The circumstances of the cited chats remain unclear; Character.AI did not immediately comment and has said user safety is its priority.
In January 2026 Character.AI and Google settled a 2024 suit over a 14-year-old's death in Florida.
quote_evidence: The document states that the service’s chatbots sometimes advised users to starve themselves, harm themselves or die by suicide, Channel NewsAsia reports.
At the same time, the circumstances in which the chats cited by the state were created remain unclear.
why_it_matters_hint: A US state is putting specific chatbot messages on the public record in a child-safety lawsuit.
event_date: Unredacted filing reported 8 Oct 2026; chats alleged from 2025
notes: Reuters page blocked here (HTTP 401). Text read at UA.News, which credits Channel NewsAsia; the Reuters headline matches the story, so the credit is kept as Reuters with the relay named. The lawsuit itself was filed in Jan 2026 with much redacted; the unredacted filing is the new event (reported 8 to 9 Oct 2026).
